subrules.rule: Each Policy card is a double-faced card. The front face has a striated textbox containing a number of policy symbols. Its illustration is vertically oriented on the right side of the card, and its typeline is along the bottom of the card. The back face is a standard Magic card.
A policy symbol is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that allows a player to take a special action.

subrules.name: 741.2a
subrules.rule: A policy symbol includes a quill icon, indicated here as {ql}.

subrules.name: 741.2b
subrules.rule: "{ql}—[Condition]" means "Any time you could cast a sorcery, you may mark this condition if [condition] and if no player has marked a policy symbol of this permanent this turn. When you do, if all of this permanent's policy abilities are marked, transform this permanent."

subrules.name: 741.2d
subrules.rule: A policy symbol may be marked even if it is already marked.

subrules.name: 741.2e
subrules.rule: A condition being marked has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that spells and abilities can identify. Once a permanent's condition becomes marked, it stays marked until it leaves the battlefield or transforms as a result of its policy symbol (see rule R741.2b). The marked designation is neither an ability nor part of the permanent’s copiable values.

mechanics.executable_reminder: Any time you could cast a sorcery, you may mark a condition of this permanent whose condition is true if no player has marked a condition of this permanent this turn. When all are marked, transform this permanent. Its marks remain until it leaves the battlefield or transforms because all conditions were marked.

semantic_equivalence.evidence: Source741.2b-e controller-only special action; repeated symbols independent; sourcewide once-turn budget persists across all faces/condition sets and control changes. Definition-scoped noncopiable marks survive ordinary transforms, clear on leaving or any successful condition-marking transform via shared status group, preserving unrelated groups.
